Rename the models of a netobject_group

Source: R/rename_models.R
rename_models.Rd

rename_models() replaces the names of the networks in a netobject_group and returns the group with nothing else changed. The names label every later report (print methods, plot panels, bootstrap and permutation output), so this is the step that turns the generic labels build_network() gives clusters ("Cluster 1", "Cluster 2") into meaningful ones ("High engagement", "Low engagement") once it is known what each cluster represents. It is the Nestimate counterpart of tna::rename_groups().

Usage

rename_models(x, new_names)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
rename_models(x, new_names)

# Default S3 method
rename_models(x, new_names)

Arguments

x

A netobject_group, or an object inheriting from it. Any other object raises an error. A net_mlvar is accepted too, but its print() and summary() find the three layers by their names (temporal, contemporaneous, between): after renaming, print() shows none of the model's dimensions and summary() fails.

new_names

The new names, a character vector in the order of the networks in x: one per network, none missing or empty, and no two the same. Anything else raises an error.

Value

An object of the same class and length as x, its networks and attributes (such as group_col) unchanged and its names replaced by new_names.

Examples

grp <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "tna",
                     actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time",
                     group = "Achiever")
names(grp)
#> [1] "High" "Low" 
names(rename_models(grp, c("High achievers", "Low achievers")))
#> [1] "High achievers" "Low achievers"
